topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

outline.topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (1 Minute)
sections.content: Briefly define a basis as a 'coordinate system'. Use a 2D grid overlay to show that any vector can be reached using basis vectors (i, j). Introduce the core question: 'How do we describe the same physical vector if we change our perspective (basis)?'
sections.example: Visualize a treasure map where the 'grid' lines are rotated. Even if the grid changes, the 'X marks the spot' location in the world remains the same.

sections.title: The Mechanism of Coordinate Transformation (1.5 Minutes)
sections.content: Explain that a coordinate transformation is essentially mapping 'Old Coordinates' to 'New Coordinates' using a Change-of-Basis Matrix (P). Visualize P as columns of new basis vectors expressed in terms of the old basis.
sections.example: Imagine a robot dog moving in a square room. If the dog's local 'forward' direction changes, we use matrix P to translate its 'local' steps into the 'global' room coordinates.

sections.title: The Change-of-Basis Formula (1.5 Minutes)
sections.content: Formulate the equation: [v]_B = P_inv * [v]_A. Use animation to show the multiplication of the matrix against the vector. Emphasize that P represents the transformation from New to Old, so its inverse is required to convert Old to New.
sections.example: Use a camera analogy: The object is the vector. The 'Old Basis' is the world frame, and the 'New Basis' is the camera's lens frame. P allows the computer to calculate where pixels appear in the camera view.

sections.title: Summary & Conceptual Application (1 Minute)
sections.content: Conclude by emphasizing that the vector v is invariant—it doesn't change; only its description changes. Reiterate that this is the mathematical foundation for computer graphics (rotating objects) and data analysis (PCA).
sections.example: Final visual: A 3D character rotating in a game engine. Show how 'Change of Basis' is what allows the game to calculate the character's limbs relative to their own body, rather than the static game world.
